A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UA-SABI research. All 16 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable. Retained equations, experiments, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original posterior recovery, calibration, and runtime experiments for the LogSin and CO2 storage models, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original MICP parameter-inference, predictive, sensitivity, and runtime analyses in Section 4.4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The core surrogate sampling procedure, training loss, and Algorithm 1 are retained. For the new MICP application, v2 omits the summary network and uses a spline coupling flow with fixed-location measurements, a limited architecture adaptation documented in Appendix C.2.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates LogSin and a virtual CO2 storage benchmark. v2 adds MICP inference from actual calcite measurements at eight locations involving four parameters. This substantially extends coverage to observational data with a mismatch between measurements and simulator predictions.

E2.justification: The corresponding LogSin and CO2 comparisons retain their comparator membership. MICP uses existing methods: low-budget ABI, SABI, Point, and E-Post; full-budget ABI is unavailable for this new case. The expanded related-work discussion does not introduce additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. The added MICP protocol uses 25 simulator evaluations, 10,000 offline training draws, and posterior comparisons without parameter ground truth. It introduces Scott-bandwidth KDE, predictive checks, and an original-versus-expanded prior comparison, increasing the k_ub upper bound from 0.0005 to 0.005. Its runtime experiment uses synthetic datasets.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix E add substantial diagnostic analyses: prior-predictive mismatch, original versus expanded priors, surrogate extrapolation, Sobol sensitivity, remaining-parameter identifiability, and posterior-predictive checks. These investigate failure conditions and uncertainty propagation beyond the retained LogSin and CO2 analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports posterior median deviations and 95% SBC confidence bands. v2 additionally reports 90% prior/posterior predictive intervals and distributions of Sobol indices for MICP. These extend uncertainty reporting; no increase in independent training repetitions or seed counts is stated.

E6.justification: The existing LogSin and CO2 result plots and runtime findings are unchanged. New MICP results show posterior concentration at the original prior boundary, dominant sensitivity to k_ub, wider predictive coverage with uncertainty-aware methods, and runtime amortization beginning at four inference runs. These are added results under new conditions, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, training objectives, and Appendix B equivalence proposition and proof are retained. Renaming the PCE index from D to J and explaining standard Sobol indices do not introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The central claim remains efficient, reliable, repeated inference for expensive simulators through uncertainty-aware surrogate training. The abstract is substantively unchanged. The new novelty paragraph makes the existing E-Post relationship explicit, while MICP adds supporting evidence for the retained contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of CO2 surrogate misspecification, MICP prior mismatch, weak parameter identifiability, and wider predictive intervals. It also explains the simplified error assumption, surrogate-complexity tradeoffs, and limitations of the low-dimensional evaluations, with additional discussion of future misspecification mitigation.

D1.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix C add MICP-specific measurement locations, priors, PCE specifications, and network choices while retaining existing implementation details. v2 also promises public code and data upon acceptance; this is a prospective disclosure, not evidence of an actual release.

R1.justification: Section 3 expands substantially beyond JANA, Bayesian neural networks, and E-Post to discuss multi-fidelity methods, sequential inference, GP surrogates, structure-aware SBI, and additional likelihood approaches. v2 also explicitly attributes its uncertainty-aware surrogate foundation to Reiser et al. and adds misspecification-related positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, method exposition, and existing case-study sequence remain largely intact. v2 makes targeted language and explanatory revisions to the introduction, objectives, and outlook, and integrates the new MICP section and appendix without reorganizing the established document structure.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template, typography, author-block layout, and figure placement, and adds eight MICP figures. Figure 2 is relabeled and repositioned, and several captions are refined. Existing result graphics are retained, including v1 Figure 7 as v2 Figure 11.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical support used simulated observations. v2 adds actual MICP measurements and investigates prior mismatch, sensitivity, and predictive coverage, substantially strengthening the assessment of practical applicability. Broader research positioning and clearer limitations further improve the paper. MICP lacks parameter ground truth and relies on prior widening, so it does not establish improved parameter accuracy, but its explicit diagnostics provide substantial additional evidence.
